prompt: Build a login page. There should be a field for the email address, a field for the password that hides what is typed, and a prominent button at the end to submit the whole thing when the user presses Enter.

samples.response:
<bl-input name="email" type="email" label="Email address" placeholder="you@example.com" required size="medium"></bl-input>
<bl-input name="password" type="password" label="Password" placeholder="Enter your password" required size="medium"></bl-input>
<bl-button type="submit" variant="primary" size="medium">Sign in</bl-button>

<form id="loginForm" class="login-form">
  <bl-input
    name="email"
    type="email"
    label="Email address"
    placeholder="you@example.com"
    autocomplete="email"
    required
  ></bl-input>

  <bl-input
    name="password"
    type="password"
    label="Password"
    placeholder="Enter your password"
    autocomplete="current-password"
    required
  ></bl-input>

  <bl-button type="submit" variant="primary">Sign in</bl-button>
</form>

<script>
  const loginForm = document.getElementById('loginForm');
  loginForm.addEventListener('submit', (event) => {
    event.preventDefault();
    const email = loginForm.querySelector('bl-input[name="email"]');
    const password = loginForm.querySelector('bl-input[name="password"]');
    const valid = email.validity?.valid !== false && password.validity?.valid !== false;
    if (!valid) return;
    // Submit the login request here.
  });
</script>

<form class="login-form">
  <bl-input
    type="email"
    name="email"
    label="Email address"
    placeholder="you@example.com"
    required
    autocomplete="email"
  >
  </bl-input>
  <bl-input
    type="password"
    name="password"
    label="Password"
    placeholder="Enter your password"
    required
    autocomplete="current-password"
  >
  </bl-input>
  <bl-button type="submit" variant="primary" size="large" label="Sign in">
  </bl-button>
</form>
